learning_outcomes.text: The student will acquire concepts related to technical representation methods and drawing dimensioning.

The student will acquire notions related to the indication of dimensional and geometric errors in industrial drawings according to ISO and ASME standards for functional dimensioning, as well as the standard for indicating surface roughness.
The student will learn common conventions for representing unified mechanical elements.
The student will acquire main notions related to parametric solid modeling and drafting to obtain 2D technical representations on the computer starting from a 3D solid model.

The student will be able to use the acquired concepts to create design solutions through graphic representation and assign dimensional and geometric tolerances to mechanical parts based on the analysis of assembly/manufacturing conditions, also indicating surface finish conditions.
The student will be able to represent common unified mechanical elements and read drawings of simple assemblies to understand the functioning of the represented devices.
The student will be able to use advanced software for creating solid models of mechanical parts and assemblies and their technical drawings.

The student will be able to interact within a work group in the conception and development phase of a product to communicate design solutions through technical representation methods using unified elements and computer-aided design.

syllabus_topics: General concepts of drawing in industrial practice
Orthogonal projections according to the first dihedral method and the third dihedral method
Views from directions not orthogonal to coordinate planes
Section with one plane and with parallel planes
Generalities on errors in manufactured parts
The ISO system of tolerances and fits
The position of tolerances in the ISO system
Elements of size and non-size elements; the size of elements and dimensional tolerance
The reference frame for part measurement
The reference frame determined by planar reference elements: construction of the reference system determined by planar faces, by planar faces and by axial elements
The reference frame determined by a first axial reference element
Qualification of planar and axial reference elements; attribution of tolerances to other part elements
Microgeometric errors and indication of surface finish state in drawings
Introduction to reading drawings; representation of assembled parts; conventional representation of common mechanical parts
Threaded elements; conventional representation of threads; threaded connecting elements
Shaft-hub connections: description and conventional representation of keys and splines
Types of rolling bearings and their conventional representation
Cylindrical and conical gears; conventional representation of gears; assemblies of speed reducers with parallel and orthogonal axes
Conception and evolution of computer-aided design systems
The concept of feature in parametric solid modeling
Description of a commercial solid modeler
Creation and definition of a sketch; creation of additive and subtractive features for solids buildable on standard planes
Construction of parallel, inclined, or tangent planes relative to existing planes
Insertion of threads, ribs, fillets, or chamfers in a solid model
Sweep and loft operations for constructing complex geometries
Construction of an assembly from components
Construction of a 2D drawing from a solid model
Creation of orthogonal views, auxiliary views, sections, and partial views
Graphic exchange formats for using 2D drawing software
assessment_rules: Learning is verified through exercises assigned during the course and an exam consisting of a written test and a computer-based test. The graphical test evaluates the correctness of technical representation and the ability to indicate dimensional and geometric tolerances based on assigned conditions. The CAD test verifies knowledge of solid modeling concepts for components, assemblies, and drafting. To pass the exam with a grade of at least 18/30, the student must demonstrate sufficient knowledge of technical representation methods, specifically orthogonal projections, sections, and dimensioning, and understand how to indicate dimensional and geometric errors in drawings. Additionally, basic knowledge of the representation of main unified elements and parametric solid modeling concepts, including the ability to create freehand technical drawings applying regulatory and unification concepts correctly and to create solid models and related technical drawings on the computer, is required.
